Rashi on Gittin 39b:10:1.hebrew: או בכסף או בשטר - תקנתו של עבד, דהא איתקוש פדיון כסף לשטר, דכתיב: "והפדה לא נפדתה או חופשה" וגו':
Rashi on Gittin 39b:10:1.english: Either via money or via a bill - [this is] the remedy for a slave, for redemption by money is juxtaposed [in Scripture] to a bill [of manumission], as it is written: "and she has not been redeemed, nor was freedom [given to her]," etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:10:2.english: And this [master] - who declared him ownerless:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:10:3.english: His monetary [hold] is abrogated - and from now on he has no remedy except through a bill [of manumission]:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:10:4.hebrew: ולאפוקי מהאי תנא - הא דאמרינן עבד ניתר בכסף, לאפוקי מהאי תנא:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:10:4.english: And to exclude [the opinion of] this tanna - This [statement] that we say, [that] a slave is emancipated through money, [serves] to exclude [the opinion of] this tanna:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:11:1.english: One might [have thought] that money completes - her emancipation, even to release [her] from prohibition:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:12:1.hebrew: אורעה כל הפרשה - כל מקרא הפרשה אורעה וסויימ' ל"לא חופשה", מדלא כתי' בסיפא "לא יומתו כי לא נפדתה או חופשה", אלא "כי לא חופשה", ש"מ כי נפדתה נמי לא יומתו, דאין בקידושין משום אשת איש הואיל ולא נכתב לה גט שחרור. וה"ק קרא: "והפדה לא נפדתה" — פדויה ואינה פדויה — "הנחרפת לאיש", כגון שפחה כנענית חציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין המאורסת לעבד עברי, שהוא מותר בשפחה ובבת חורין, הבא עליה באשם; דאי לא נפדתה כלל אין כאן אשם, ולכך הוזכרה פדיה, ולא משום דאי נפדתה לגמרי יהו קידושיה קדושין והבא עליה במיתה, דמדכתב סיפא "לא יומתו כי לא חופשה", משמע אורעה דין מיתתה בחיפוש השטר, ואפילו נפדתה כולה בלא שטר אין בה מיתה. והא דכתיב "לא נפדתה", רבותא אשמעינן, דאע"ג דלא נפדתה כולה אלא חציה איכא אשם:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:12:1.english: The entire portion is linked - The entire scriptural passage is linked and concluded with [the phrase] "nor was freedom [given her]," since it is not written at the end [of the verse] "they shall not be put to death, because she was not redeemed or given freedom," but rather "because she was not given freedom." Learn from this that even if she was redeemed [with money], they are not put to death, because there is no [full] betrothal [with respect to the prohibition] of a married woman, since a bill of manumission was not written for her. And this is what the verse means: "And she was not at all redeemed" — [meaning] she is partially redeemed and partially unredeemed — "who is designated for a man," such as a Canaanite maidservant who is half-maidservant and half-freewoman, who is betrothed to a Hebrew slave (who is permitted [to cohabit] with a maidservant and with a freewoman) — one who cohabits with her [is liable] for a guilt-offering; for if she had not been redeemed at all, there would be no guilt-offering here, and for that reason redemption was mentioned, and not because if she were completely redeemed her betrothal would be [a full] betrothal and one who cohabits with her [would be liable] to death. For since the end [of the verse] writes "they shall not be put to death, because she was not given freedom," it implies that the law of her death penalty is linked to the freedom of a bill [of manumission], and even if she was completely redeemed without a bill, there is no death penalty for [cohabiting with] her. And that which is written "she was not redeemed" teaches us a novel point: that even though she was not completely redeemed, but only half of her, there is [liability for] a guilt-offering:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:12:2.hebrew: גומר בה - מוציאה לגמרי, בין משעבוד בין מאיסור:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:12:2.english: Completes her [emancipation] - [A bill of manumission] releases her completely, both from servitude and from prohibition:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:12:3.hebrew: ואין כסף גומר בה - דאינו מוציא אלא מידי שעבוד, אבל לא מידי איסור שפחה, שיהו קדושין תופסין בה:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:12:3.english: And money does not complete her [emancipation] - for it only releases [her] from servitude, but not from the prohibition of a maidservant, such that betrothal would take effect with her:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:14:1.english: Of a house of prayer - [That is,] the synagogue:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:14:2.hebrew: אמר לו אני הייתי אומר אין הלכה ורבנן דאתו כו' - נחלקו עלי ואמרו דר' זירא משמיה דרב נחמן אמר הלכה:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:14:2.english: He said to him: I would say [the] halakha is not [in accordance with his opinion], and the Rabbis who came, etc. - [They] disagreed with me and said that Rabbi Zeira in the name of Rav Nachman said [the] halakha is [in accordance with his opinion]:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:15:1.english: And when I came - I [came] to Sura, I found him, etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:15:2.hebrew: אימא לי איזי גופא דעובדא - דרב נחמן, דשמעינן מינה דאמר "הלכה", היכי הוה:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:15:2.english: Tell me, izi [my friend], the incident itself - of Rav Nachman, from which we heard that he said "halakha [is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon]," how did it happen:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:16:1.hebrew: מאן דחזא - סבר משום דהלכה כרבי שמעון, שהיו סבורין שאלו חליפין הן בקנין סודר, דקונה ככסף, דכתיב "שלף איש נעלו" (רות ד׳:ז׳), ולא אמר כלום — דרב נחמן להתירה לישראל קאמר כר' שמעון, אבל מידי שעבוד יצאת:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:16:1.english: One who saw [it] - thought [that Rav Nachman ruled this way] because the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, for they thought that this [throwing of the hat] was chalifin [exchange] through kinyan sudar [acquisition by kerchief], which acquires like money — as it is written, "a man drew off his shoe" (Ruth 4:7) — and [yet Rav Nachman ruled that] it had no effect, for [they assumed] Rav Nachman was speaking with respect to permitting her to [marry] an Israelite, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, whereas from subjugation she had [already] exited:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:16:2.hebrew: ולא היא - לא כדברי האי דאמר לי דרב נחמן אמר הלכה, אלא אין הלכה קאמר, כדאמינא מדעתאי, והכא אף מידי שעבוד לא יצאת:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:16:2.english: But that is not so - [It is not like] what he told me, that Rav Nachman said the halakha [follows Rabbi Shimon]; rather, he said the halakha does not [follow him], just as I said on my own; [and in this case,] she has not even left servitude.

Rashi on Gittin 39b:16:3.hebrew: דהוה ליה כליו של מקנה - וקי"ל בפרק הזהב (ב"מ מז:) דהלכתא כרב דאמר בכליו של קונה, ומשום דברי שכיב מרע ליכא, שהרי לא צוה כמוסר לבניו להקנותה לעצמה במתנת שכיב מרע, אלא בקנין זה נתכוין לשחררה, והרי הוא טעות:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:16:3.english: For it was the vessel of the one transferring ownership - And we hold in Chapter HaZahav (Bava Metzia 47b) that the halakha is in accordance with Rav, who says [that acquisition is effected] with the vessel of the recipient. And [emancipation] on account of the words of a dying person does not apply here, for he did not command [them]—as one instructing his sons—to grant her to herself as a gift of a dying person; rather, he intended to emancipate her through this act of acquisition, and it is an error:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:1:1.english: Did you hear it explicitly - from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:1:2.hebrew: מאי כללא - מאיזה כלל יש לי ללמוד, דקבעית מינאי "מכללא שמיע לך":
Rashi on Gittin 39b:1:2.english: What inference - From which general principle do I have to learn [it], that you ask me, "Did you hear it by inference?"

Rashi on Gittin 39b:1:3.english: I have despaired - It is an expression of renunciation of ownership:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:1:4.hebrew: אין לו תקנה - בבת ישראל ולא בשפחה, שהרי משוחרר הוא קצת ואינו גמור:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:1:4.english: He has no remedy - [neither] with an Israelite woman nor with a maidservant, for he is partially emancipated and not completely [free]:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:2:1.hebrew: מה אשה - אם הפקירה בעלה, לא התירה לינשא לאחר בכך, עד שיתן גט:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:2:1.english: Just as a wife - If her husband declared her ownerless, he has not thereby permitted her to marry another [man] until he gives [her] a bill of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:3:1.hebrew: וקא דייקת מינה - כיון דרבי מאשה יליף, לא איירי רבי אלא במפקיר עבד גדול שיש לו יד לקנות עצמו, ומשהפקירו אין לו עליו אלא איסור אבל לא ממון — כאשה זו שגט שלה אינו בא להפקיע ממון שיש לו עליה אלא איסור; אבל בעבד קטן לא איירי רבי, דלאו דומיא דאשה הוא, דאיכא דררא דממונא עליה, ובדידיה סבירא ליה דיש לו תקנה בשפחה, דלא קנה עצמו בהפקר:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:3:1.english: And you deduced from this - Since Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] derives [his ruling] from a wife, Rabbi is speaking only of one who declares ownerless an adult slave, who has the legal capacity to acquire himself, so that once he has declared him ownerless, [the master] has upon him only a prohibition [barring him from marrying a Jewish woman], but not a monetary [claim] — like this wife, whose bill of divorce does not come to release a monetary [claim] that [the husband] has upon her, but rather a prohibition. But regarding a minor slave, Rabbi did not speak, for he is not comparable to a wife, since there is a monetary aspect [still] upon him; and regarding him, [Rabbi] holds that he has a remedy through a [Canaanite] maidservant, since he does not acquire himself through ownerlessness:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:4:1.hebrew: ואי מכללא - ילפינא, מאי קשיא לך בגוה, דאצטריך לך למיבעי "בפירוש או מכללא":
Rashi on Gittin 39b:4:1.english: And if [it is] by inference - [that we] learn [it], what difficulty do you have with it, that you needed to ask, "[Did you hear it] explicitly or by inference"?

Rashi on Gittin 39b:4:2.hebrew: אמר ליה - אי מכללא שמיע לך, לאו שפיר דייקת:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:4:2.english: He said to him - If you heard [it] by inference, you did not deduce [it] properly:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:4:3.hebrew: דוק מינה להאי גיסא מה אשה בין גדולה בין קטנה - התרתה בגט, אף מפקיר עבדו דאיירי ביה רבי, בין גדול בין קטן קאמר, ודומיא דאשה הוא להך גיסא:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:4:3.english: Deduce from it to this side: Just as a woman, whether [she is] an adult or a minor, - her release is with a bill of divorce, so too, [regarding] one who declares his slave ownerless, which Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] was discussing, he is speaking of both an adult and a minor [slave], and [a slave] is comparable to a woman in that respect:

Rashi on Gittin 39b:5:1.hebrew: אין לו תקנה אלא בשטר - כאשה, השתא משמע דעבד אינו ניתר אפי' בפדיון:
Rashi on Gittin 39b:5:1.english: He has no remedy other than via a bill [of manumission] - like a woman [who can only be released by a bill of divorce]; at this point, it implies that a slave is not released even through redemption:

Tosafot on Gittin 39b:15:1.hebrew: אמר להן לא עשה ולא כלום - פירש בקונט': משום דדברי שכיב מרע ככתובין וכמסורין דמו ליכא, שהרי לא צוה כמוסר לבניו להקנותה לעצמה, אלא בקנין זה נתכוון לשחררה, והרי הוא טעות. ולא שייך להזכיר כאן מתנת שכיב מרע, דהויא ליה במקצת; ולמצוה לקיים דברי המת איכא לדמויי, אם היה כמוסר לבניו:
Tosafot on Gittin 39b:15:1.english: He said to them: He did nothing - Rashi explained: There is no [effect] on account of [the principle that] the words of a person on his deathbed are considered as written and delivered, for he did not give an instruction in the manner of one transmitting [instructions] to his children to transfer her to herself; rather, he intended to emancipate her through this act of acquisition, and it is an error. However, it is not relevant to mention here a gift of a person on his deathbed, since it is [a gift of] a portion [of his property]; rather, it could be compared to [the principle that] it is a mitzva to fulfill the words of the deceased, had he been [speaking] as one transmitting [instructions] to his children:

Tosafot on Gittin 39b:16:1.hebrew: משום דהוה ליה כליו של מקנה - אבל אם היה כליו של קונה, היתה זוכה עצמה בחליפין, דתני' בהדיא בפ"ק דקידושין (דף כב:) דעבד כנעני נקנה בחליפין, משום דחליפין דמו לכסף, וכל היכא דכסף קני, חליפין נמי קני, לבר מאשה, משום דבפחות משוה פרוטה לא מקניא נפשה, כדאמר בריש קדושין (דף ג.). ומכאן יש להוכיח דהלכה כרב, דאמר בכליו של קונה בפרק הזהב (ב"מ מז:). ועוד אמרינן התם: במנא דכשר למקנייה ביה, לאפוקי מדלוי. ולא דמי להא דאמר בפרק המגרש (לקמן גיטין פה:) דאתקין רבא "מיומא דנן ולעלם" לאפוקי מר' יוסי, דאמר זמנו של שטר מוכיח עליו, אע"ג דרב גופיה פסיק כוותיה בההיא פרקא; דהתם לשופרא דשטרא אתקין, אבל הכא, למאן דאמר בכליו של מקנה, לא מהני בכליו של קונה. ובקונטרס פירש בהזהב (ב"מ מז.) דלוי, דאמר בכליו של מקנה, כ"ש בכליו של קונה. ואין נראה, כיון דאמר דגואל נתן לבעז, לא מהני אלא בענין זה; כמו לרב נחמן, דאמר פירי לא עבדי חליפין, משום דבעינן דומיא ד"נעלו", ולא אמרינן דהואיל דכלי שוה פרוטה קני, כל שכן פירות שוים אלף זוז, דאיכא הנאה טפי דגמר ומקני. ועוד אמרינן בנדרים בהשותפין (דף מח:) דסודרא קני — על מנת להקנות הוא:
Tosafot on Gittin 39b:16:1.english: Because it was the utensil of the one who transfers ownership - However, if it had been the utensil of the one who acquires, she would have acquired herself [i.e., her freedom] through chalifin [exchange], as it is explicitly taught in the first chapter of Kiddushin (22b) that a Canaanite slave is acquired through chalifin, because chalifin resembles money, and wherever money acquires, chalifin also acquires — except for a woman, because for less than the value of a perutah she does not transfer herself [in betrothal], as [the Gemara] says at the beginning of Kiddushin (3a). And from here one can prove that the halakha follows Rav, who says [that chalifin is performed] with the utensil of the one who acquires, in the chapter [entitled] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 47b). Furthermore, we say there: "[with a utensil] that is fit to acquire with it" — to exclude [the view] of Levi. And this is not similar to that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] HaMegaresh (below, Gittin 85b), that Rava instituted [writing in a bill of divorce] "from this day and forever" to exclude [the view] of Rabbi Yosei, who says the date of a document proves [when it takes effect], even though Rav himself rules in accordance with him in that chapter — for there, [Rava] instituted it for the enhancement of the document, whereas here, according to the one who says [that chalifin is performed] with the utensil of the one who transfers ownership, it is not effective with the utensil of the one who acquires. And in the Kuntres [Rashi] explained in [the chapter entitled] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 47a) that [according to] Levi, who says [it is performed] with the utensil of the one who transfers ownership, all the more so [is it effective] with the utensil of the one who acquires. But [this] does not seem [correct]: since he says that the redeemer gave [his shoe] to Boaz, it is only effective in this manner — just as according to Rav Nachman, who says produce does not effect chalifin, because we require [something] similar to "his shoe," and we do not say that since a utensil worth a perutah acquires, all the more so produce worth a thousand zuz [should acquire], where there is greater benefit such that he resolves and transfers ownership. Furthermore, we say in Nedarim, in [the chapter entitled] HaShutafin (48b), that a scarf acquires [because] it is [given] on condition to transfer [ownership]:

Tosafot on Gittin 39b:3:1.hebrew: מה אשה איסורא ולא ממונא - וא"ת: היאך עבד משתחרר בשטר לאבא שאול אם לא יפקירנו תחלה, דמה אשה איסורא ולא ממונא אף כו'? וכי תימא דלשון הכתוב בשטר, כגון "הרי את בן חורין", "הרי את לעצמך", הוי לשון הפקר — אם כן, לשמואל למה לי שטרא? יפקירנו! ועוד, דאפי' על ידי הפקר היאך משתחרר קטן לאבא שאול? ואור"י, דדוקא בקנין דמיתה דילפינן מאשה אמרי' איסורא ולא ממונא דומיא דאשה; אבל שטר, שכתוב בהדיא בקרא "או חופשה לא ניתן לה" (ויקרא יט), משוחררת בשטר לחודיה, דמקרא מלא דיבר הכתוב. ועוד, דאיתקש שטר לקנין כסף, דכתיב (שם) "והפדה לא נפדתה", ועיקר קנין כסף מפקיע ממון, כדאמר הכא: "נתייאשתי מפלוני עבדי" — אין לו תקנה אלא בשטר, אבל בכסף לא, דפקע ליה כספיה מכי אפקריה:
Tosafot on Gittin 39b:3:1.english: Just as a wife [is released from] a prohibition but not a monetary [bond] - And if you ask: How can a slave be emancipated by a document according to Abba Shaul if [the master] does not first declare him ownerless, since "just as a wife [is released from] a prohibition but not a monetary [bond], so too [a slave]," etc.? And if you say that the wording written in the document — such as "Behold, you are a free man," [or] "Behold, you belong to yourself" — constitutes a declaration of ownerlessness, if so, according to Shmuel, why do I need a document? Let him [simply] declare him ownerless! Furthermore, even through a declaration of ownerlessness, how could a minor [slave] be emancipated according to Abba Shaul? And Rabbeinu Yitzḥak says that specifically with regard to acquisition through death, which we derive from a wife, do we say "[it releases] a prohibition but not a monetary [bond]," similar to a wife. However, [regarding] a document, which is written explicitly in the verse, "or freedom was not given to her" (Leviticus 19[:20]), she is emancipated by a document alone, for the verse stated a complete statement. Furthermore, a document is compared to acquisition by money, as it is written (ibid.), "and she has not been redeemed," and the primary [effect of] acquisition by money is to release monetary [ownership], as [the Gemara] says here: [If one says,] "I have despaired of so-and-so, my slave" — he has no remedy except through a document, but not through money, because his monetary [right] was already terminated from the time he declared him ownerless:
